the β-carbons of the polypeptide poly-γ-metyl-L-glutamate are in position 1 and that the polypeptide is in the form of the α-helical structure.
poly-γ-methy-L-glutamate has an α-helix structure with eighteen residues in a turn of 5.1 Å and that the β-carbons are in position 1,2 rather than in 1,3.
the X-ray diffraction pattern of poly-γ-m-methyl-L-glutarate is that of an α-helix with 18 residues in five turns, and that the β-carbons are in position 1 rather than position 2.

the following points: (1) the determination of the structure of a synthetic polypeptide, poly-γ-methy-L-glutamate; (2) the assignment of the β-atom to position 2 rather then position 1; (3) a comparison of the structure of this synthetic polypeptide with that of serum albumin; (4) a comparison of these two proteins with the structure of the synthetic polypeptide poly-γ-L-glutamate.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the β-carbons are in position 1 and the α-carbon atoms in position 2, and that the polypeptide chain is folded into a helix.

the X-ray diffraction evidence indicates that the polypeptide chain is in an α-helix conformation, that the side chain of the glutamyl residue occupies the position of the β-carbons, that there is a hydrogen bond between the α-amino and α-carboxyl groups, and that the α-amino group is hydrogen-bonded to the carbonyl oxygen of a residue in the next turn of the helix.
the polypeptide chain of poly-γ-metyl-L-glutamate, like that of the protein molecules, is a helical structure in which the β-carbon atom of each amino acid residue occupies position 2 of the helix.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the polypeptide chain of the α-helical region is essentially a right-hand spiral, with the C=O group at position 1, the α-carbon atom at 2, the β-carbon atom at position 3, the N atom at 4, and the CαH group at 5.

the α-helix has been confirmed for a synthetic polypeptide, and the β-carbon atom has been assigned to position 2 for both the α-helix and serum albumin.

it is not possible to determine the positions of the α-carbon atoms in a helix by means of radial distribution functions.
